Market Context: RTM prices are highly volatile due to grid stress events and renewable intermittency. 13.1% of all 15-min blocks hit the price cap zone (>Rs9,000). The market shows a clear downward trend from Rs5,181/MWh (2023) to Rs3,751/MWh (2025), driven by increasing renewable energy penetration.

📈 Price Time Series Overview

Figure 1: Full RTM MCP time series (15-min) with daily average and 30-day rolling volatility.

Key Observation: Clear regime shifts across years. High price spikes are clustered during evening peak hours (7–10 PM). Rolling volatility shows periods of high market stress corresponding to grid congestion or generation outages.

📉 Price Distribution Analysis

Figure 2: Left — Bimodal distribution (normal trading + spike zone). Right — Year-over-year box plots showing regime shift.

Bimodal Distribution: Main cluster around Rs3,550/MWh (normal) and secondary cluster near Rs10,000–12,000 (cap events). This bimodality makes MAPE challenging as spike predictions carry high uncertainty.
Regime Shift Confirmed: Box plots by year show systematic downward shift in prices. 2023 distribution is entirely different from 2025–2026, validating the 18-month training window decision.

🔬 STL Decomposition Analysis

STL (Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS) separates the time series into three interpretable components: Trend (long-term direction), Seasonal (recurring patterns), and Residual (unexplained shocks).

Weekly STL — Daily Average MCP (period = 7 days)

Residual (Unexplained)

Figure 3: STL decomposition on daily MCP. Trend shows long-term price decline. Seasonal captures weekly demand cycle. Residuals = price spikes.

STL Interpretation: The Trend confirms gradual price decline (renewable penetration effect). The Seasonal component captures weekly demand cycle — weekdays see higher prices than weekends. The Residual contains price cap spikes — the high residual variance (29.1%) explains why MAPE ~20% is the realistic performance ceiling for this market.

Daily STL — 15-Minute Blocks (period = 96 blocks = 24 hours)

Figure 4: STL on 15-min data. Period=96 captures within-day price cycle. Evening peak (blocks 68–80 = 5–8 PM) consistently elevated.

15-Min STL Insight: The daily seasonal component shows the characteristic double-peak — morning peak (6–9 AM, industrial startup) and stronger evening peak (6–10 PM, domestic + commercial load). The trend at this resolution captures weekly demand cycles.

🕐 Seasonal Pattern Analysis

Figure 5: MCP patterns by hour, day of week, and month. Heatmap reveals price hotspots at evening hours x weekdays.

Peak Hours: Hour 19:00 (evening) shows highest avg prices (Rs6,817/MWh). Hour 13:00 shows lowest prices (Rs2,462/MWh) driven by solar generation.
Weekend Effect: Saturday and Sunday show ~8–12% lower prices as industrial demand drops. This weekly pattern is captured in the STL seasonal component and drives the day_of_week feature importance.

📐 Stationarity Analysis (ADF Test)

Figure 6: Rolling mean/std for original and differenced series. ADF test table and Q-Q normality check.

ADF Result (Original): Statistic=-4.9767, p-value=0.0000 → Series is stationary
ADF Result (First Difference): Statistic=-11.4828, p-value=0.000000 → Stationary after differencing. Confirms ARIMA(p,1,q) structure. XGBoost handles non-stationarity implicitly through lag features.

📡 Autocorrelation Analysis (ACF / PACF)

Figure 7: ACF and PACF for original and first-differenced daily MCP. Significant spikes at lag 7, 14 confirm weekly seasonality.

Key Lags:
Lag 1 (1 day): Strong — yesterday's price is best predictor (confirms mcp_lag_24h importance)
Lag 7 (1 week): Significant spike — same-day-last-week pattern (weekly seasonality)
Lag 14 (2 weeks): Secondary harmonic
PACF: Drops after lag 1–2, suggesting AR(1)/AR(2) structure for ARIMA baseline

⚡ Price Spike Analysis

Figure 8: Left — Hourly frequency of price cap events. Right — Price percentile distribution showing heavy right tail.

Price Cap Events: 13.1% of blocks hit the cap zone (>Rs9,000). Spikes concentrated in evening hours (7–10 PM). These events require real-time grid data unavailable in our dataset — a structural explanation for why MAPE cannot reach <5%.

📅 Year-over-Year Regime Analysis

Figure 9: Left — YoY hourly price profiles showing regime shift. Right — Annual average MCP decline trend.

Regime Shift Finding: 27.6% price decline from 2023 to 2025. Training on 2023 data to predict 2025–2026 caused MAPE to spike from 20% to 160%+. Limiting training to last 18 months keeps train and test in the same market regime.

Weather Correlation Analysis

Figure 10: MCP correlation with temperature, wind speed, and humidity (Delhi).

Temperature shows positive correlation (cooling demand). Wind speed shows negative correlation (more renewables = lower prices). These validate including weather features in the model.

Commodity Price Correlation

Figure 11: MCP correlation with crude oil, natural gas, and USD/INR exchange rate.

Crude oil and natural gas show moderate positive correlation — thermal generation costs pass through to market prices. As renewables penetration grows, correlation with fossil fuel prices is weakening.
